notes: The independent audit changes only the geometry of two existing insertion leaders. The new paths remove an unsupported long return branch while preserving the source attachment points, raised wording and the separate de r leader. These findings merge into D12 and D18, retaining both original C/H omission flags.

The first superscript in relation (7) is retained as i,j at medium confidence. In the existing relation7 crop, the short low mark between the separately dotted i stem and the long j has white gaps on both sides. Its position and independence support the comma rendering despite its short, nearly oval shape. This is a local ink decision; punctuation in later superscripts was not used to supply it.

The two arrowheads in (8) and (9) are compact but genuinely headed in the existing arcs crop. The additional terminal comma in the source exponent of (8), the live i left of the cancelled (9) index cluster, and the differing looped sigma in (7) versus tau in (10) remain as read; no algebraic normalization was made.

The lower marginal groups remain physically separated. In particular, si on bouche / R_r^i, is not silently transferred into the following parenthetical NB, and neither independently visible si is suppressed to make a grammatical sentence.

The short glyph before Z/3Z in the first marginal note can resemble a colon. Comparison with the same-page correspondant à l’orientation occurrence in the existing sommets crop shows the same small low angular body and detached upper mark; à is retained. This comparison supports a narrowly scoped hand observation, not a universal punctuation rule.

All ten prior unresolved readings remain qualified. The review did not recover the first fully obscured cancelled word before repère opposé, determine the old (9) cluster beyond +2|i+2, or settle the raised verb, short cancelled words, marginal attachment, or double-contoured C.
